object: Hilbert second-seat verification of Riemann's Q-qual proof (rt6_qqual_unconditional_proof.md)
lemma1_diagonal_lb: VERIFIED correct: D_t >= (1/4)logN via one-prime-two-composite, PNT+Selberg, unconditional
lemma2_offdiag_ub: VERIFIED correct BUT SCOPED: proves |C|=O(1) ONLY for distinct-6-offset pairs
GAP: the fixed-s sector contains SHARED-OFFSET pairs (two distinct triples at sum s share <=1 offset value). At s=36: 74/300 = 25% of off-diagonal pairs share an offset. Lemma 2 does NOT cover them.

shared_pair_behavior.note: shared site repeats -> a dLambda^2 in C -> log-enhanced numerator

why_it_matters: proof bound for 1-shared: |C|~logN over proven D>=(1/4)logN => R=O(1), NOT o(1). Strengthening the diagonal to (logN)^{1+eps} needs a TWO-prime lower bound = Hardy-Littlewood/twin-prime, UNPROVABLE. So the naive patch hits the twin-prime barrier.
verdict: Theorem as written ('R->I entrywise') is NOT established: ~25% of entries (shared-offset) are only unconditionally O(1), not o(1). Empirically they ->0 (R1: 0.057->0.034), so TRUE but UNPROVEN by the stated lemmas.
UNCONDITIONAL_FIX: Lemma 3 (shared-offset closure). A fixed-s pair shares AT MOST ONE offset a. Factor u_t=dLambda_a*v_t, u_t'=dLambda_a*v_t', v=product of the 2 non-shared sites. Since dLambda_a^2>=0 it is a valid weight: R[t,t']=E_w[v_t v_t']/sqrt(E_w[v_t^2]E_w[v_t'^2]), w=dLambda_a^2. The 4 non-shared sites are ALL DISTINCT (<=1 shared), so the reduced numerator E_w[v_t v_t'] is a 4-distinct-site correlation = O(1) by Lemma-2-machinery one order down (conditioning on n+a prime adds only a bounded singular-series factor), while E_w[v_t^2]>= c*logN by Lemma-1-machinery one order down. => R = O(1/logN) -> 0 UNCONDITIONALLY. One reduction suffices because fixed-s => <=1 shared.
net: Lemmas 1,2 correct; theorem needs Lemma 3 to cover the shared-offset quarter; with Lemma 3, Q-qual IS unconditional and full-matrix. Without it, unconditional only on the distinct-offset block.
